EVERYTHING AGENTS NEED TO KNOW
==============================

For maintainers and the AI agents they start. Read this first in a new
session that has no earlier context, then AGENTS.md, then
.github/DECISIONS.md and .github/RELEASING.md.

This file is not part of the programs, the release archives or the
documentation, and "git archive" and GitHub's source downloads leave it
out (.gitattributes). The repository is public, so this file holds no
secret, no customer data and no real company name. Keep it that way.


1. WHAT THE PROJECT IS
----------------------

numb-form fills section A of the "Appendix A - Risk Assesment" form
for every company in an overview spreadsheet that has no folder yet.
A person confirms every document. Three programs work in a chain:

  numb-form    makes a folder and a filled form per new company
               (mode = direct writes into the working folder;
               mode = review works on a copy in Downloads).
  numb-commit  review mode only: copies the accepted folders from the
               copy in Downloads back into the real working folder.
  numb-date    copies the date of each form into the "Report created"
               column of the spreadsheet, after the person accepts.

Read docs/usage.md, docs/numb-date.md and docs/configuration.md for
what a person sees. Go standard library only; no third-party modules.


2. RULES THAT ARE NEVER BROKEN
------------------------------

* Never merge into main. The owner merges every pull request.
* Never change a pull request's release tag (the "vX.Y.Z:" at the start
  of its title). The text after it may change.
* Never force-push, rebase or amend a pushed branch. Use merge commits.
* Never commit customer files, logs, run folders, private notes or real
  company names. Examples use made-up names such as "Foo GmbH".
* Never add online lookups for companies, web search or scraping.
* Never test locally; tests run on GitHub (AGENTS.md, "Changing the
  code"). Compile checks are fine.
* Never edit docs/es or docs/de; the translate workflow writes them.
* Keys and tokens only from environment variables, never in files.
* Ask the owner before anything hard to undo or visible outside the
  repository.


3. HOW A CHANGE IS MADE
-----------------------

* One release is one pull request, titled "vX.Y.Z: what it changes".
  Patch for fixes, minor for features (.github/RELEASING.md).
* A change to what a person sees updates its manual page and CHANGES.md
  in the same pull request. scripts/check-changes.sh fails otherwise.
* Files stay short, about 300 lines at most.
* Every template format implements form.Filler, splices bytes instead
  of re-serialising, passes form.Verify, and has tests and fuzz targets.
* New GitHub Actions are pinned to a full commit SHA with the version as
  a comment. Python tools are pinned with hashes.
* Before pushing, run the compile checks:

    sh scripts/check-deps.sh && test -z "$(gofmt -l .)" && for os in linux windows darwin freebsd openbsd netbsd; do GOOS=$os go vet ./... || exit 1; done

* Branch names: claude/<topic>, for releases claude/vX.Y.Z-<topic>.


4. THE RELEASE STACK
--------------------

Many releases are prepared at once as a stack of pull requests: each
release branch starts from the previous one, and each pull request's
base is the previous release's branch. The owner merges them in order,
oldest first, with "Create a merge commit" (never squash or rebase).

After the owner merges one:

1. GitHub retargets the next pull request to main and tries to rebase
   it. Because the stack uses merge commits, that rebase often fails and
   the pull request shows a conflict ("dirty").
2. Fix: merge origin/main into the next branch with a merge commit. Keep
   the branch's own files; take main's docs/es and docs/de (main gains a
   translation commit after every merge). Check that only translations
   differ from the branch before the merge.
3. Merge that branch forward into every later branch, one merge commit
   each, and push without force.
4. Cancel the CI runs the push started on the later branches (see 5).

A new release in the middle of the stack: branch it from the release
before it, open its pull request against that branch, merge it into
the next release's branch, retarget the next pull request's base to the
new branch, and merge forward to the end of the stack.

"Dormant" code: large features land in parts over several releases.
Code without a caller ("Nothing uses it yet. No change in behaviour.")
is expected until the release that switches it on. Dead-code tools list
it; that is not a bug.


5. CI
-----

Workflows (.github/workflows):

  ci                 lint, tests (Linux, macOS, Windows), BSD virtual
                     machines, containers, every cross-compile target;
                     on every pull request, push and night.
  security           gosec, govulncheck, CodeQL, fuzzing, zizmor,
                     history scan; on every pull request, push and night.
  formats            LibreOffice format tests; every pull request, push
                     and night.
  translate          writes docs/es and docs/de; overlapping runs cancel
                     each other, so re-run one at a time.
  release-approval   after a merge: waits for the owner's approval.
  release            on a tag: archives, checksums, signatures, image.
  edge               the rolling build (release tag "edge").
  updates            daily checks for newer tools and Go.
  scorecard          OpenSSF scorecard.

Runners are limited. Let CI run on one pull request at a time: cancel
the runs a push starts on later branches, and re-run them in order once
the earlier pull request is green.

Read results without a browser:

    sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD) && curl -s "https://api.github.com/repos/z4dm42f5kp-ux/numb-form/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha" | grep -E '"(name|status|conclusion)"'

A failure is never "a flake" without proof. Never skip, disable or
quarantine a test to get green.


6. THINGS THAT BREAK EASILY
---------------------------

* Windows drops trailing dots and spaces in folder names, and refuses
  reserved names (CON, NUL, COM0-COM9, LPT0-LPT9, COM1-3 and LPT1-3
  with superscript digits). fsutil.SafeName handles them; tests must
  use the names SafeName gives.
* macOS may write file names decomposed ("u" + combining mark instead
  of "ü"). textutil.MatchKeys handles it.
* Paths with umlauts, long paths and read-only folders must work on
  every system.
* The spreadsheet in "3. Übersichten" is never written, except by
  numb-date (dates only) after the person agrees.
* Section B and everything outside section A is never touched, and no
  formatting is ever added.
* The standard texts for missing values are spelled exactly as in
  AGENTS.md, including their spelling mistakes.


7. FIRST STEPS IN A NEW SESSION
-------------------------------

1. git fetch, then list the open pull requests and their bases; find the
   oldest unmerged one in the stack.
2. Check that pull request: mergeable? CI green on its head? If it
   conflicts, follow section 4.
3. Read the open issues; a "vX.Y.Z Plans" issue lists what the owner
   wants in that release.
4. Keep the owner's standing rules from section 2. When unsure, ask.
